description: The bar chart illustrates the perplexity of a model across different sparsity rates, with two sets of bars representing "Per-Output" (blue) and "Per-Input" (orange) metrics. The x-axis displays the sparsity rate, ranging from 10% to 80% in 10% increments, while the y-axis shows perplexity on a logarithmic scale, spanning from 1 to 1000. For each sparsity rate, the "Per-Output" and "Per-Input" values are shown as adjacent bars. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 40%), both metrics are relatively low, with "Per-Output" values around 1 and "Per-Input" values slightly higher, around 2. As the sparsity rate increases, both metrics rise, with "Per-Output" values increasing more sharply. At 80% sparsity, the "Per-Output" value reaches approximately 500, while the "Per-Input" value is slightly higher, around 800. The chart indicates that increasing sparsity leads to a significant increase in perplexity, with the "Per-Input" metric consistently showing higher values than "Per-Output" across all sparsity rates.
